title: Venus Pipes & Tubes Ltd - 543528 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Venus Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores, with EBITDA margin at 16.3% and PAT up 7% to INR25.4 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores and FY26 revenue grew 22% to INR1,166.8 crores. Export sales fell to INR87.8 crores from INR112.5 crores on Middle East disruption, while domestic demand stayed robust. The company completed its seamless and welded capex program and announced a spooling foray for data centers backed by a INR185 crores LOI. Management guided to more than 20% growth in FY27 and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, rising to 18% by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY vs INR41.6 crores; margin vs 16.1% in Q4 FY25
down from INR112.5 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: 59% of Q4 FY26 revenue, growing 18% YoY; FY26 volume growth above 15%. Seamless utilisation was 90-95% for FY26 and similar in Q4.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: 34% of Q4 FY26 revenue, growing 15% YoY; FY26 volume growth around 10%. Utilisation was around 60-65% for FY26 and similar in Q4.

segments.name: Others / fittings / spooling
segments.commentary: 7% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Fittings capacity commenced operations on 3 June 2026; spooling facility (capex around INR70 crores) targeted for commercial production by mid Q3 FY27 and full operation by December 2026.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 exports INR87.8 crores, down from INR112.5 crores YoY, but still above 30% of revenue. FY26 exports grew 18%; current order book is about 40% export.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20%, including pipes, fittings and spooling; management says this is kept within current geopolitical assumptions.
EBITDA margin in FY27 to be higher than FY26's 16.3%, moving to about 17% and then 18% blended by FY28; management says the intent is to improve every quarter.
FY27 consolidated capex guided at INR90-100 crores.
Export share guided at 30-35% going forward.
Spooling business targeted at about 3x asset turn, with EBITDA margins above the current base business; management did not confirm a 35% margin benchmark cited by an analyst.
Working capital guided at about 120 days of sales, with no major change expected for new data-center business.
capex_capacity: Capex program fully commissioned: installed capacity 27,600 MTPA welded pipes and 20,400 MTPA seamless pipes, plus fittings capacity.

Seamless expansion raised from 4,800 to 6,000 MTPA: 1,800 MTPA operational November 2025 and 4,200 MTPA operational on the day of the call (26 May 2026). Company is now 100% backward integrated for mother hollow on the 20,400 MTPA seamless capacity.
Total capex on seamless, welded and fittings for the expansion is more than INR200 crores; at full utilisation, asset turn is at least around 3x.
Spooling and fabrication facility with fittings machinery, capex around INR70 crores; trial runs by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production by mid Q3 FY27.
Tandem JCO press installed for longer welded pipes (INR12 crores); management says capacity is largely unchanged and the gain is in SKU range and tender eligibility.
Acquired 15 acres of adjacent land for future expansion.
demand_pricing: Order book INR450 crores excluding a INR185 crores data-center LOI, which management says is from a single data-center customer and is executable in about 15 months.
Separately, the company is L1 on BHEL tenders worth about INR50 crores, expected to be awarded in 30-45 days; less than 60% of the existing BHEL order had been executed by Q4.
Management cited about INR685 crores of total visibility (order book, LOI and BHEL L1), about 30% export, giving visibility for the next 2-3 quarters.
Domestic demand cited from CNG, power, oil and gas, engineering and chemicals; new approvals reported from oil and gas in the US and Middle East.
Middle East orders are currently weak; management expects recovery if the conflict eases.
Pricing rose 5-7% in FY26, partly grade mix; management expects RM cost increases to flow through and says a prolonged period of high RM prices may weigh on margins.
EBITDA per tonne in FY26 about INR65 per kg (totality basis; blended figure not given).

qa_highlights.question: When will the spooling business start, what revenue and margin does it carry, and how long will the INR185 crores order take?
qa_highlights.answer: Target start by end of calendar 2026 with about 3x asset turn and higher margin than the base business; the order is executable in about 15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of at least 20%, and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, moving to 17% and then 18% by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the PAT stay flat at INR25-26 crores over about nine quarters despite the investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT growth should follow as most capex is complete, with the value-added projects expected to lift PAT in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% FY27 growth guidance at risk given a lower order book (INR450 crores vs about INR575 crores a year ago) and softer exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the BHEL L1 orders, the data-center LOI, new fittings, and the expanded seamless capacity to 6,000 MTPA; it said FY26 was harder yet grew 22%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the spooling business differ from Ratnamani's, and could it enter nuclear spooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ratnamani focuses on nuclear spooling, while Venus targets data-center spooling. Nuclear entry has limitations but is a possible long-term goal. It declined to give a margin estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the BHEL order flow?
qa_highlights.answer: BHEL tenders are expected to open from August to September, with more orders in Q2 FY27, and BHEL is working to expedite delayed orders.

risks_watch: Export softness from the Middle East conflict; Q4 exports fell about 22% YoY and management says Middle East order flow has not yet recovered.
Raw material and gas cost inflation; management warned that prolonged high RM prices may affect margins.
Spooling execution: trial runs, commercial start timing (mid Q3 FY27), and the dependence on a single LOI customer.
Order book fell to INR450 crores (vs about INR575 crores a year earlier); the 20% FY27 growth guidance depends on new orders and BHEL tenders.
Welded pipe utilisation of only 60-65% for FY26, despite the welded capacity being unchanged.
Cash conversion: EBITDA to CFO was 59% in FY26; PAT has been flat at about INR25-26 crores for about nine quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the data-center opportunity, but cautious on exports and raw material costs. Management was often vague on spooling unit economics, utilisation per tonne and margins, deferring to one-on-one calls.
key_quotes: I am proud to share that entire capex program has now been fully commissioned.
So, at least for next 2 to 3 quarters, we have the good visibility from Europe market, US market as well as from domestic market.
It is like PEB for piping, you can say.
